Heard Sri Ankit Singh, holding brief of Sri Shailesh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Shyam Dhar Maurya, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2. As informed by learned AGA, notice to the informant has been served on 29.08.2024 but none is present on behalf of the informant.

3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 76 of 2024, under Sections 376(2)(n), 313, 342 I.P.C. and Section 5(j)(ii)/6 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Saurikh, District Kannauj, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: The applicant is stated to be employed in a private firm at Bhiwadi, district-Alwar, Rajasthan.
The victim aged about 15 years is stated to be also employed there whereby the applicant is stated to have committed rape with her thereby impregnated her.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT :
5.
The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has nothing to do with the said offence.
6. The FIR is delayed and there is no date and time of the offence mentioned in it.
7. The instant FIR has wrongly been instituted at Kannauj as the offence had been committed within the jurisdiction of police station Bhiwadi, District-Alwar, Rajasthan.
8. The victim by her looks seems to be major, although her date of birth as per school certificate of class-III is stated to be 10.05.2009.
The said certificate cannot be taken into consideration in the light of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 9. There are ample contradictions in the statements of the victim recorded under section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. to the FIR.

The date of offence has bee introduced in her statement recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C. whereby it is stated to be 08.12.2023 but the same has been changed in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. to be 08.01.2024.
10. Even the medical report does not corroborate the prosecution story.
11. The pregnancy test is stated to have been found positive at the time of her urine examination but the same has not been corroborated by the ultrasound report.
12. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
13. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 04.03.2024.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail

,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE :
14. The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:

sentences.text: , the Supreme Court has observed that in the absence of records relating to the birth of the victim, no other documents except the Matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination board or certificate by a corporation, municipal authority or a Panchayat can be relied upon to ascertain the age of the victim.
16. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

17. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
18.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
19.
Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
20. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

21. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

22. Let the applicant- Shani involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to Shani vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82801256/
3 treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

entities.text: Shani vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 23. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

24. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
